data.content_ref: inline:The experiment cannot actually discriminate the two hypotheses as claimed. The 'redundant Batcher' hypothesis says a 45-net is extractable as a subnetwork of Batcher's 48-net, but greedy single-comparator removal (remove one comparator at a time, keep only if sorting is preserved) is an incomplete search for subnetworks: a valid 45-comparator subnetwork may require removing a set of comparators that are individually load-bearing — removing any one alone breaks sorting, yet removing the correct combination preserves it. In such a case greedy pruning stalls above 45 (e.g., at 47 or 48), which the claim would interpret as supporting 'structural barrier,' when in fact the 45-net is a subnetwork and 'redundant Batcher' is true. Thus the experiment conflates greedy-heuristic failure with structural necessity: only reaching ≤45 falsifies structural barrier, but failing to reach ≤45 does not confirm it. The counterconditions acknowledge ambiguity only at exactly 46 and single-order sensitivity, leaving the deeper incompleteness of single-removal unaddressed, so the claimed discrimination is invalid.
